Messages.Author: Charles Richard Robb
Messages.Body:
If you pplay pulling strings during a vote, can it cancel the initial 1
vote value of the main vote card?

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3ks16i$m...@NNTP.MsState.Edu>,

Charles Richard Robb <cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu> wrote:
>If you pplay pulling strings during a vote, can it cancel the initial 1
>vote value of the main vote card?

No, the vote card always counts as a vote for itself. While the
vampire calling it performed the action, votes directly from political
actions are not considered to be from a particualr vampire.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu (Charles Richard Robb) writes:

>If you pplay pulling strings during a vote, can it cancel the initial 1
>vote value of the main vote card?

Yes. That vote DID come from the pulled vampire, so it is cancelled.

cr...@Ra.MsState.Edu (Charles Richard Robb) writes:

>If you play pulling strings during a vote, can it cancel the initial 1

>vote value of the main vote card?

Pulling Strings cancel's a vampire's vote, but the political card gives a
vote to the Methuseleh (not the minion). So, no.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
curt...@aol.com (CurtAdams) writes:





Tom Wylie: When a vampire plays a card that grants a vote, the vote is
considered to have come from both the vampire and the Methuselah
(answer to a question on the card that taps vampires who vote vs. the
card that forces Methuselahs with dissenting votes to pay pool).

The PA that called the vote counts as a vote from the vamp, so it will
be cancelled. Any PA cards burned for additional votes do not come
from a vamp, so would not be cancelled.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
js...@discus.ise.vt.edu (Joseph Cochran) writes:

>In article <3kuiga$l...@redwood.cs.scarolina.edu>,
>L. Scott Johnson <sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu> wrote:
>>Rulebook: The card used to call a vote provides one vote for the Meth.
>>Obvious (?) effect: That vote comes from the acting vampire as well.
>>
>>Rulebook: The Edge and PA cards may be burned for one vote each.
>>Obvious Effect: Since no vampire was involved with playing the card/gaining
>> the vote, then the vote comes from the Methuselah only.

> One more data point. Rulebook: A political card always provides
>one vote for the Methuselah playing it.
>Later in that section: In addition to the vote provided by the card
>played, you get the following extra votes for vampires under your
>control.
> Both of these would seem to indicate that the vote comes
>straight from the card.
The rulebook also seems to indicate that votes gained from titled vamps
come from the control of the vamp, not the vamp itself. But this is
(also) not the case.

Rulebook: Controlling a Prince provides 2 vote for the Methuselah.
Rulebook: Playing a PA card to call a Referendum provide a vote for the Meth.

Design Team: The vote comes from both the vampire and the Methuselah.

Simplicity (always the way to go):
If you need a Minion to get the vote, then the vote comes from that minion.

This includes: titled votes, action mods, reactions, and the initial PA.
This does not include: subsequent PAs nor the Edge.

Is there a simple rule-of-thumb which explains why the PA played by a
vampire would not count as being played by that vampire? (while
allowing the remainder of the votes to be played as explained by DT).

I can't think of one.

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
js...@discus.ise.vt.edu (Joseph Cochran) writes:

>In article <3kth5r$h...@redwood.cs.scarolina.edu>,

>L. Scott Johnson <sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu> wrote:

>>Tom Wylie: When a vampire plays a card that grants a vote, the vote is
>>considered to have come from both the vampire and the Methuselah
>>(answer to a question on the card that taps vampires who vote vs. the
>>card that forces Methuselahs with dissenting votes to pay pool).

> Right, that applies to action mods and reactions. That was what
>Tom specifically referred to. The question then becomes do actions fall
>under that ruling?
> My initial reaction is to say that they do not.

Tom "specifically" referred to nothing except votes gained from titled
vampires, actually. (And that only because that was the example used).

Action Mods and Reactions are obvious extensions (since they require
a Minion to play).

The initial PA is also an obvious (IMO) extension, since it requires a
vamp to play.

--------------------------------
BTW, this is the full extent of my argument, so rather than create another
what time did WotC impose a card limit on MtG :-), I will content myself
to simply reading your (and anybody else's) followups. I understand
the points you have made, and I agree that the Design Team has left this one
(minor) point unclarified. I would have no problem playing it the way
you suggest, but I do beleive that it is not the proper way to interpret
it, neither in terms of game mechanics nor in terms of game concept.
